hero.name: Saqib Ali
roles: Ground Station Engineer @ Orbitalink pvt Ltd
hero.lede:
Model it, simulate it, build it, measure it, then fix whatever the measurement showed.
I design motor drives and satellite antenna tracking systems, and take them through to tested hardware.

about.heading: Where control, hardware and RF meet
paragraphs: A control law that works in Simulink and one that works on a real motor are not the same thing. Most of my work lives in the gap between them.

At **Orbitalink** I lead the antenna tracker: a 435 MHz cross-Yagi, a Fusion 360 chassis stiff enough to hold a beam on a moving satellite, motion firmware for hybrid servo drives, and adaptive control for a mount heavy enough to fight back.

At **IIT Ropar** I built a five-phase IPMSM drive from the transforms up — two current planes instead of one, five regulators instead of three, and a torque equation I had to derive before I could use it. Then I put the modulator on a TI C2000 DSP and tested the gate driver.
Electrical Engineering at **Zakir Husain College of Engineering and Technology, AMU**.

items.org: Indian Institute of Technology Ropar · Rupnagar
bullets: Modelled a five-phase IPMSM in MATLAB/Simulink and designed dual-plane FOC.
Generated ePWM on a TI C2000 DSP in Code Composer Studio and tested the gate driver circuit.
Lead end-to-end development of a two-axis satellite antenna tracker, from chassis and RF to firmware.
Designed a 435 MHz cross-Yagi in MMANA-GAL with a phasing harness for circular polarisation.
Wrote firmware for NEMA23 hybrid servos on HSD57 drivers; porting it to STM32F411.

items.org: Orbitalink, with AMU Innovation Foundation · Aligarh

Built the tracker chassis model and two-axis PID positioning logic; support satellite tracking and equipment calibration.
